newsitem.title: USA: US album sales rose in first half of 1997-Soundscan.
newsitem.headline: US album sales rose in first half of 1997-Soundscan.

text.p: U.S. album sales rose 5.4 percent in the first half of 1997, marking a turnaround for the $12 billion music industry, whose sales have been flat for the past two years, Soundscan Inc. said Thursday.
U.S. stores sold 288 million albums from January though June, compared with 273.4 million in the year-ago period, said the Hartsdale, N.Y.-based company, which monitors retail music sales.
A Soundscan spokeswoman said U.S. album sales showed strong growth in the first quarter as well, rising 8.6 percent to 147.7 million units from a year ago.
Sales were led by the Spice Girls, the British female pop group, which sold 2.7 million copies of its debut album on EMI Group Plc's Virgin label, she said.

The band Na Doubt, which is signed with Interscope, also sold strongly. Interscope is half-owned by Seagram Co. Ltd.'s Universal Music Unit and the singer Jewel, who is on Time Warner Inc.'s Atlantic label.
Among the world's six big music labels, Warner Music remained the U.S. market share leader with 18.75 percent of the U.S. album market, Soundscan said.
